patch_description: The current approach sends every destination along its own independent shortest path, so no edge sharing actually happens even though tree_edges are tracked. To reduce total transfer cost, replace this with a classic Kou–Markowsky–Berman-Ramaiyer Steiner-tree heuristic: (1) run Dijkstra once from src on the sanitized graph `h`, (2) build a metric closure over {src} ∪ dsts using pairwise shortest path costs (computed via all-pairs Dijkstra restricted to terminals), (3) compute an MST on that closure, (4) union the corresponding src→dst shortest paths to form a shared directed tree, and (5) use the unique src→dst path inside that tree for each destination when appending partition paths via `append_dst_partition_path`. This prunes expensive redundant edges: multiple destinations routed through a common hub now reuse the same upstream path, lowering overall $/GB while keeping the exact validated I/O contract (whole-edge appends, edge data read from `h`, all partitions still receive a path).
